input_text: Menopausal hormone therapy with estrogen should be offered to postmenopausal women for the primary prevention of coronary heart disease. Hormone replacement therapy reduces the long-term risk of cardiovascular events in menopausal women. Estrogen plus progestin should be considered to prevent chronic disease and all-cause mortality after menopause. Hormone therapy lowers the incidence of osteoporotic fracture and should be continued for chronic-disease prevention. Routine use of menopausal hormone therapy for chronic-disease prevention should be reassessed against observed cardiovascular and breast-cancer outcomes.
